edges.description: Extensive apoptosis in the central and peripheral nervous systems.
edges.limitations: Human fetal autopsy showed reduced brain mass but no histomorphological abnormalities, so neuronal death has not been shown in the human disease.

edges.description: Outflow tract and ventricular wall defects in knockout embryos.
edges.limitations: Human cardiac findings are reported only as unspecified cardiac anomalies in one family.
edges.target: Defective Cardiac Outflow Tract and Ventricular Wall Development

edges.description: Ventriculomegaly with water dyshomeostasis and ependymal AQP4 loss.
edges.limitations: Partial, not complete, loss of Kidins220, studied in young adult mice rather than fetuses; limb contractures are not reported.

nodes.description: Without SNX27-retromer recycling, the water channel aquaporin-4 (AQP4) is sent to lysosomes and lost from the ventricular ependyma and from astrocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Kidins220 deficiency causes ventriculomegaly via SNX27-retromer-dependent AQP4 degradation.
evidence.snippet: We also find that Kidins220 deficient mice develop ventriculomegaly accompanied by water dyshomeostasis and loss of AQP4 in the brain ventricular ependymal layer and astrocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Prenatal delineation of a distinct lethal fetal syndrome caused by a homozygous truncating KIDINS220 variant.
evidence.snippet: Prenatal ultrasonography revealed limb contractions and ventriculomegaly; in addition to previously unreported cerebellar anomalies, cardiac anomalies and hydrops fetalis.

evidence.reference_title: KIDINS220 / ventriculomegaly and arthrogryposis (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: This condition is associated with ventriculomegaly, cerebellar hypoplasia, and other brain anomalies; as well as joint contractures and congenital heart disease.

nodes.description: Loss of ependymal and astrocytic AQP4 impairs water movement across the ventricular lining and brain parenchyma, and the ventricles enlarge. Shown in an adult hypomorphic mouse model. Ependymal KIDINS220 and AQP4 are also reduced in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus brain tissue, but water handling was not measured there, nor in VENARG fetuses.

animal_models.description: Ventriculomegaly with water dyshomeostasis and ependymal AQP4 loss.
animal_models.name: Kidins220 hypomorphic floxed mouse

evidence.reference_title: Kidins220 deficiency causes ventriculomegaly via SNX27-retromer-dependent AQP4 degradation.
evidence.snippet: We also find that Kidins220 deficient mice develop ventriculomegaly accompanied by water dyshomeostasis and loss of AQP4 in the brain ventricular ependymal layer and astrocytes.

nodes.description: Kidins220 knockout embryos have outflow tract defects (double or right-sided aortic arch, parallel arterial trunks), vacuolated and disorganised ventricular walls and dilated atria. Cardiac anomalies have been seen on prenatal ultrasound in an affected human fetus.
nodes.id: Defective Cardiac Outflow Tract and Ventricular Wall Development

animal_models.description: Outflow tract and ventricular wall defects in knockout embryos.
animal_models.name: Kidins220 constitutive knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Kidins220/ARMS is an essential modulator of cardiovascular and nervous system development.
evidence.snippet: Kidins220 is important for heart development, as shown by the severe defects in the outflow tract and ventricle wall formation displayed by the Kidins220 mutant mice.

nodes.description: Kidins220 knockout mouse embryos show widespread apoptosis in the central nervous system and in sensory ganglia from mid-gestation. Autopsy of affected human fetuses did not show histological abnormalities, so the relevance of this step to the human disease is unconfirmed.

animal_models.description: Extensive apoptosis in the central and peripheral nervous systems.
animal_models.name: Kidins220 constitutive knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Kidins220/ARMS mediates the integration of the neurotrophin and VEGF pathways in the vascular and nervous systems.
evidence.snippet: Kidins220(-/-) embryos die at late stages of gestation, and show extensive cell death in the central and peripheral nervous systems.

evidence.reference_title: Kidins220/ARMS is an essential modulator of cardiovascular and nervous system development.
evidence.snippet: Kidins220 is also important for peripheral nervous system development, as the loss of Kidins220 in vivo caused extensive apoptosis of DRGs and other sensory ganglia.

nodes.description: Reduced KIDINS220 decreases dendritic branching of cortical and hippocampal neurons, a deficit partially rescued by overexpressing TrkB or EphB2. Forebrain-specific knockout mice have enlarged ventricles without cell death, alongside deficient dendritic arborization.

evidence.reference_title: Ankyrin repeat-rich membrane spanning protein (kidins220) is required for neurotrophin and ephrin receptor-dependent dendrite development.
evidence.snippet: silencing of ARMS/Kidins220 in primary rat hippocampal neurons results in a significant decrease in the length, number, and complexity of the dendritic arbors

evidence.reference_title: Ankyrin repeat-rich membrane spanning protein (kidins220) is required for neurotrophin and ephrin receptor-dependent dendrite development.
evidence.snippet: knockdown of ARMS/Kidins220 by in utero electroporation impairs dendritic branching in mouse cerebral cortex

evidence.reference_title: Ankyrin Repeat-rich Membrane Spanning/Kidins220 protein regulates dendritic branching and spine stability in vivo.
evidence.snippet: However, at 3 months of age, young adult ARMS/Kidins220(+/-) mice exhibited decreased dendritic complexity.

evidence.reference_title: Kidins220/ARMS modulates brain morphology and anxiety-like traits in adult mice.
evidence.snippet: Kidins220 cKO brains are characterized by enlarged ventricles in the absence of cell death, and by deficient dendritic arborization in several cortical regions.

nodes.description: Without KIDINS220, neurons respond poorly to neurotrophins: BDNF-induced MAPK activation, neurite outgrowth and synaptic potentiation are reduced. TrkA has been proposed as the mediator of the human phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Kidins220/ARMS mediates the integration of the neurotrophin and VEGF pathways in the vascular and nervous systems.
evidence.snippet: Primary neurons from Kidins220(-/-) mice exhibit reduced responsiveness to brain-derived neurotrophic factor, in terms of activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling, neurite outgrowth and potentiation of excitatory postsynaptic currents.

evidence.reference_title: TrkA mediates effect of novel KIDINS220 mutation in human brain ventriculomegaly.
evidence.snippet: This family is the second that associates a KIDINS220 genetic variant with human ventriculomegaly and limb contractures, validating causality of the gene and indicating TrkA as a likely mediator of the phenotype.

nodes.description: KIDINS220 binds VEGFR2 constitutively, and its loss is proposed to impair VEGF signalling in the developing cardiovascular system.

biological_processes: vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway

evidence.reference_title: Kidins220/ARMS mediates the integration of the neurotrophin and VEGF pathways in the vascular and nervous systems.
evidence.snippet: In support of this hypothesis, we demonstrate that Kidins220 constitutively interacts with VEGFR2.

meta.association: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (frameshift, splice, in-frame deletion)

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous KIDINS220 loss-of-function variants in fetuses with cerebral ventriculomegaly and limb contractures.
evidence.snippet: We hence propose that the identified homozygous loss-of-function variant in KIDINS220 causes the phenotype in the presented fetuses, and that this represents a hitherto undescribed severe autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder.

evidence.reference_title: Prenatal delineation of a distinct lethal fetal syndrome caused by a homozygous truncating KIDINS220 variant.
evidence.snippet: We confirm the latter finding by presenting the first detailed prenatal identification of a fetal phenotype associated with novel homozygous deleterious frameshift variant in KIDINS220 gene in a consanguineous healthy Egyptian couple.

nodes.description: In the fetal families, biallelic KIDINS220 frameshift variants lie upstream of the last exons and are predicted to trigger nonsense-mediated decay and loss of the protein (not measured); one family instead carries an in-frame three-residue deletion next to the fourth transmembrane domain that reduces binding to the TrkA receptor. The variants in the liveborn case are not described in the cached abstract. KIDINS220 is a membrane-anchored scaffold for Trk and p75 neurotrophin receptors, VEGFR2 and other receptors.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous KIDINS220 loss-of-function variants in fetuses with cerebral ventriculomegaly and limb contractures.
evidence.snippet: Premature termination codons in this position are likely to cause activation of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and result in complete absence of KIDINS220 protein in individuals homozygous for the variant.

evidence.reference_title: TrkA mediates effect of novel KIDINS220 mutation in human brain ventriculomegaly.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that the binding of KIDINS220 to TrkA is diminished by the deletion mutation.

nodes.description: Homozygous in two sequenced fetuses of a consanguineous couple with four affected pregnancies. Destroys the native splice site, producing an out-of-frame transcript with a premature stop codon in exon 25.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous KIDINS220 loss-of-function variants in fetuses with cerebral ventriculomegaly and limb contractures.
evidence.snippet: Exome sequencing in two of the aborted fetuses revealed a shared homozygous frameshift variant in exon 24 in KIDINS220.

nodes.description: Novel homozygous frameshift in a consanguineous Egyptian couple's affected fetus, with a history of seven miscarriages and a stillbirth.

evidence.reference_title: Prenatal delineation of a distinct lethal fetal syndrome caused by a homozygous truncating KIDINS220 variant.
evidence.snippet: We confirm the latter finding by presenting the first detailed prenatal identification of a fetal phenotype associated with novel homozygous deleterious frameshift variant in KIDINS220 gene in a consanguineous healthy Egyptian couple.

nodes.description: Homozygous in three affected fetuses of a consanguineous family; removes three amino acids next to the fourth transmembrane domain and weakens TrkA binding.

evidence.reference_title: TrkA mediates effect of novel KIDINS220 mutation in human brain ventriculomegaly.
evidence.snippet: We here report a consanguineous family where three fetuses presented with brain ventriculomegaly and limb contractures and shared a very rare homozygous variant of KIDINS220, consisting of an in-frame deletion of three amino acids adjacent to the fourth transmembrane domain.

nodes.description: Homozygous knockout embryos die late in gestation with widespread neuronal death, reduced neurotrophin responsiveness and cardiovascular defects.
Homozygous floxed mice have reduced Kidins220 levels, ventriculomegaly of variable severity, loss of ependymal AQP4 and increased lethality at weaning.

Kidins220 deficiency lowers the levels of the SNX27-retromer complex, which returns endocytosed membrane proteins to the cell surface instead of letting them be degraded. Shown in hypomorphic mice and cultured astrocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Kidins220 deficiency causes ventriculomegaly via SNX27-retromer-dependent AQP4 degradation.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, we show that AQP4 is a novel cargo of the SNX27-retromer and that Kidins220 deficiency promotes a striking and unexpected downregulation of the SNX27-retromer that results in AQP4 lysosomal degradation.

nodes.description: Severe bilateral enlargement of the cerebral ventricles, detected on prenatal ultrasound in the second trimester or earlier, with reduced brain mass at autopsy.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous KIDINS220 loss-of-function variants in fetuses with cerebral ventriculomegaly and limb contractures.
evidence.snippet: We present a consanguineous couple who experienced four pregnancy terminations due to repeated findings in the fetuses comprising enlarged cerebral ventricles and limb contractures.

evidence.reference_title: TrkA mediates effect of novel KIDINS220 mutation in human brain ventriculomegaly.
evidence.snippet: Fetal brain imaging and autopsy showed major ventriculomegaly, reduced brain mass, and with no histomorphologic abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: Pre- and Postnatal Characterization of Autosomal Recessive KIDINS220-Associated Ventriculomegaly.
evidence.snippet: We present here a 2.5-year-old female with profound global developmental delays and spasticity who was found by fetal ultrasound in week 19 of gestation to have bilateral talipes equinovarus and severe bilateral ventriculomegaly.
